thread:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — we've got three major asks from customers re: the Optimize toolkit: per-model quantization suggestions, auto-batching defaults, and eval-triggered regression alerts.
Chris Patel: Do we have severity/impact breakdown? Which is blocking revenue?
Leo Gómez: Enterprise customers pushing for alerts + SLAs. Also several smaller startups asked for quant recs to cut costs.
Sarah Owens: From support: quant recs + canned evals reduce churn more than batching defaults. but batching affects unit cost dramatically at scale.
Maya Chen: Thinking prioritization: 1) Eval-triggered alerts (SLO safety) 2) Quant rec engine 3) Batch/caching UX tweaks. Open to debate.
Chris Patel: How big is the engineering lift for eval alerts? endpoints, triggers, notification infra?
Leo Gómez: Rough estimates: infra plumbing 2w, eval integration 1w, alert config UI 1w. Total ~4w for an MVP.
Maya Chen: Proposed MVP scope for alerts: - hook existing eval runs -> auto-create alert if eval metric drops >X over baseline - send to Slack/email + create incident in Ops tool - simple rollback suggestion to previous model
Sarah Owens: Rollback suggestion is huge for customers. But louder ask: must be per-route promptset mapping. otherwise noisy.
Chris Patel: For quant recs: we can repurpose part of the model profiler. MVP: recommend pair (quant config, expected token cost delta, expected quality delta) per model+workload.
Leo Gómez: Also need audit logs for compliance (customers request). Make logs part of MVP for both features.
Maya Chen: Launch criteria proposal: - Alerts: 95% true-positive threshold on internal evals, <10% noise rate in canary group - Quant recs: within 5% of expected latency/cost in benchmark suite - UX: toggles for on/off + basic audit trail
Sarah Owens: Can we ship alerts to hosted first, then Dedicated/private in next phase? Customers prefer hosted but Dedicated customers need on-prem alerting too.
Chris Patel: Agree staged rollout. Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private because private needs KMS/HSM and air-gap support.
Maya Chen: Tradeoffs: If we push quant rec engine earlier, we can save customers $$$ quickly but alerts reduce risk. Which has higher ROI short-term?
Leo Gómez: ROI: quant recs have immediate measurable cost saving; alerts are more about retention for large customers. Recommend do quant recs in parallel with a small alerts MVP.
Maya Chen: Ok action items: - Chris: scope infra changes for alerts + estimate infra deps (due: 3/29) - Leo: draft quant rec algorithm doc + benchmarking plan (due: 3/26) - Sarah: collect top 5 customer promptsets for canary (due: 3/24)
optimize-bot: Reminder: new product sync scheduled Thu 10am. Add "Optimize ops priorities" to agenda.
Chris Patel: noted. One more question: metrics we'll track for launch: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/second, cost/token, eval-regression-rate. Anything else?
Maya Chen: add "user-facing incidents" (count of app-level errors attributed to model degradation), and customer NPS flag for canary cohort.
Sarah Owens: I'll also prepare sample Slack alert templates and escalation steps.
Leo Gómez: I'll prototype a simple quant recommendation snippet:
```
model: redwood/efficient-7B
workload_profile: short-chat
quant_suggest: int8/q4_0
expected_cost_reduction: 34%
expected_quality_delta: -1.5% (perplexity)
```
Maya Chen: Love it. Let's review in Thu sync. If no objections by EOD Friday, I'll move these into the roadmap and tag as Q2 stretch work.
Chris Patel: 👍
Sarah Owens: +1
Leo Gómez: 👍
